irac.issue: Whether the State of Orissa can levy a tax on the sale of goods within the state if the sale is made in the course of inter-state trade, and whether the Orissa Sales Tax Act, 1947, is valid in this regard.
irac.rule: The Constitution of India, Article 301, Article 304, and the Orissa Sales Tax Act, 1947.
irac.application: The Supreme Court held that the Orissa Sales Tax Act, 1947, as amended, is valid and that the State of Orissa can levy a tax on the sale of goods within the state, even if the sale is made in the course of inter-state trade, subject to certain conditions.
irac.conclusion: The Supreme Court upheld the validity of the Orissa Sales Tax Act, 1947, and allowed the State of Orissa to levy tax on the sale of goods within the state, even in the course of inter-state trade.
